Inside Meghan Markle’s life as an ‘involved’ school mom to Archie and Lilibet — surrounded by security

By
Leah Bitsky
Published Nov. 25, 2026, 8:02 a.m. ET

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Trading royal duties for parenting duties.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 11:13
Instaread

Meghan Markle and Prince Harry are extremely involved in the day-to-day lives of their two kids, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, as they settle into their new UK community, a source exclusively told Page Six.

“Meghan and Harry are there for the school drop-off and pick-up every single day. They are always accompanied by security,” the insider shared.

Explore More

Meghan Markle’s hairstylist reveals glimpse inside duchess’ new life at home with Prince Harry after UK return

Prince William plans to strip Prince Harry, Meghan Markle and their kids of royal titles when he ascends the throne: report

Secret reason for Prince Harry and Meghan Markle’s sudden move back to UK finally revealed 

We’re told the Duchess of Sussex, 45, is making a “real effort” to get to know other parents at their kids’ school.

“She introduced herself on the kids’ first day and has been getting involved with as much as she can,” the source shared.

Meanwhile, we’re told the Duke of Sussex, 42, is “a little bit more reserved,” with the insider claiming, “He doesn’t seem as open and friendly as she’s been.”

The source noted that Archie and Lilibet’s attendance at the school came as a “complete surprise to everyone.”

“The parents of children who are in their classes were just told that ‘an English boy and an English girl who have been living in California will be joining the class,'” the source divulged.

In a shock move, the Sussexes moved with their children back to the UK in August after living in California for six years upon resigning from their royal responsibilities.

While Harry initially shared that they moved so his kids could experience a British education and be closer to family, sources told Page Six last week that their relocation could be visa-related.

“His visa expired and wasn’t immediately renewed,” one US government source told us at the time, while other sources made similar claims.

While the details of Harry’s exact visa type have yet to be revealed, a former State Department official previously told us, “All visas have expiration dates and regularly need to be renewed; that could explain their sudden departure to England.”

Page Six also reported that Harry and the As Ever founder plan on spending Thanksgiving with their kids in Britain, but will travel back to the States for Christmas so Lili and Archie can celebrate with Markle’s mom, Doria Ragland.

Meghan and Harry had a warm welcome from UK locals during their first official joint public appearance since their return across the pond in October. However, they were quickly dragged back into the headlines later that month when Meghan’s father, Thomas Markle Sr., was accused of possessing a trove of child pornography.

Earlier this month, he was arrested in Florida on child porn charges. Days later, he was hit with a slew of charges in the Philippines over child sex abuse material.

Join the Conversation
Have your say.Share your thoughts in the comments below.

Meghan, who has been estranged from her father since at least 2018, has remained relatively silent on the matter, aside from a statement she made when the accusations first came to light.

“I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children was for one reason: to protect them,” she said in part. “I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families.”

The “With Love, Meghan” host said she was “deeply distressed” over the allegations, which she was made aware of some years prior.

Page Six has reached out to the Sussexes’ rep for comment.
